title: Who was the first Brazilian in space?
hook: A hundred years after the 14-Bis, a Brazilian went to the space station.
summary: Marcos Pontes was Brazil’s first astronaut: he flew to the International Space Station in 2006, on the Centenary Mission.

cardBlocks.text: On the night of 29 March 2006, Brasília time, a Russian Soyuz spacecraft lifted off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan for the International Space Station (ISS). Alongside Russian Pavel Vinogradov and American Jeffrey Williams sat Marcos Pontes, Brazil’s first astronaut.

The flight was named the Centenary Mission, marking a hundred years since Alberto Santos Dumont flew the 14-Bis aeroplane. It was made possible by an agreement signed in October 2005 between the Brazilian Space Agency and Russia’s Roscosmos. Pontes took about 15 kilograms of cargo with instruments for scientific experiments from Brazilian institutions.
Marcos Pontes became the first Brazilian in space in 2006, on the Centenary Mission to the International Space Station.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Pontes was chosen in 1998, when a space station agreement gave Brazil the right to nominate a candidate for the US space programme. By the eve of the flight, he had been training as an astronaut for eight years. After the deal with Russia, he prepared at Star City, the cosmonaut training centre.
The experiments used weightlessness to study its effects on enzymes, proteins, DNA and several kinds of seeds.
